rules.statement: TL-UL host drivers in this library are not required to drive valid signals LOW for at least 100 cycles during reset, unlike the TileLink 1.7.1 requirement.
TL-UL devices tolerate shorter reset windows than the TileLink-specified 100 cycles.
All request steering to a device must be a function of the address only; a_source and a_user do not enter into address calculation.
A host may use source ID bits to ascribe request identifiers, since TL-UL does not guarantee in-order responses.
The fabric architect must ensure AIW is large enough for outstanding host requests plus maximum source ID growth added by bus primitives.

rules.condition: when converting from a host such as AXI using RID or WID
rules.statement: The fabric must provide enough host ID bits to maintain the converted host ID values.

rules.condition: when a bus primitive adds source ID bits
rules.statement: The primitive shifts incoming a_source left and post-pends its sub-source bits.

rules.condition: when the response returns through a primitive that added sub-source bits
rules.statement: The sub-source bits are shifted off with zeros shifted into the top, and the result is returned on the originator's d_source.
Assertions should be in place to ensure no significant bits of a_source are lost in M:1 sockets.
Hosts may only use the low bits of the source identifier and must not assume all AIW bits are returned intact.
A device must return the associated a_source value on the response d_source.
Bus hosts and devices must understand the usage of user bits and apply them appropriately.
User bits follow the same timing as source ID bits: a_user matches a_source and d_user matches d_source.
The bus fabric must not rely on user bits for transport and should pass them on blindly; user bit usage is assigned project-wide.
a_opcode designates Get (3'b100), PutFullData (3'b000) or PutPartialData (3'b001); for PutPartialData, a_size gives 2^a_size bytes and a_mask should mark valid byte lanes.
a_size should be 'h2 for a 32b write.
TL-UL hosts should not assert non-contiguous a_mask values, only a restricted set of masks.

rules.condition: device does not support a subword mask
rules.statement: A device may assert d_error if it does not support a given contiguous or non-contiguous subword mask.
Bus devices should return an error for undefined request opcodes.
Undefined d_opcode values should return an error.
